readout_other: Pressure algometry pain detection threshold (Wagner FPX-25); cold pressor task tolerance
direction_notes: Pain detection thresholds and cold pressor tolerance increased after median nerve stimulation versus baseline and sham; the effect lasted about 8-9 hours.

exposures.label: Median nerve at the antecubital fossa, wearable concave transducer

target.label: median nerve in the antecubital fossa

device.model: PerNeUS concave PZT transducer (DL-47); driven by IGT BBBoq or custom battery circuit

timing.protocol_description: 650 kHz bursts of 200 ms (BD) gated 5 ms on / 5 ms off (50% duty cycle, repeated 20 times), burst repetition frequency 100 Hz, delivered every 2 s (inter-stimulus interval) for a total sonication duration of 5 min; the fully wearable device was described as 136 repetitions every 2 s.

flags.reason: Burst rule: the paper calls 200 ms the burst or pulse duration (and says a 5 ms pulse is emitted), while 50% duty cycle at 100 Hz implies 5 ms pulses; 5 ms recorded as the pulse and 200 ms as the train.
Recorded 0.2 s for one 200 ms burst; the paper's 'sonification duration' of 5 min is the whole session (repeated every 2 s). The 136 repetitions at 2 s would give about 4.5 min, not 5 min.
Paper names 100 Hz both a pulse repetition frequency and a burst repetition frequency.

Isppa 41.4 W/cm2 is given in the Discussion as measured; acoustic characterisation was done in a deionised water tank but the sentence does not name the domain. A pressure of about 0.57 MPa at 30 V is also given but is not tied to the stimulation setting.

Separate experiments used 8 (commercial driver, PA), 8 (CPT), 4 + 4 (wearable circuit), 4 + 4 (duration) and 3 (hydrogel durability) volunteers; overlap between experiments is not stated. Recorded as the list of experiment sizes taken from the text ([8,4,4,4,4,3]), quote shows n=8 only.
Transducer built in-house from a Del Piezo PZT element; driven by an IGT BBBoq system in the commercial-driver experiments and a custom circuit otherwise.
Sham stimulation is mentioned as randomised and counterbalanced but not described.
Outcome is increased pain threshold (authors infer inhibition of nociceptive signalling).
Protocol states median nerve localised at the antecubital fossa; pain thresholds were measured at the hand.
